title: The bishop(?) of Fermo to Sforza Attendolo, Naples, 10 March 1413: a royal marriage offer, wholly in cipher (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 12, DECODE R4790)

steps.what: siena1421 survey: R4790 and R1858 images downloaded with the DECODE cookie; no. 12 inventoried as a whole letter in graphic signs with word separators and 'taken as read' from R1858's Decrypted status (no reading attempted, not counted).
George Lasry (report): transcription by Claude from the images, refined by him in CTTS; 865 cipher symbols, 95 word dividers.
George Lasry (report): key recovered by Claude's own simulated annealing on the 865 symbols, ciphertext only.

George Lasry (report): key refined; reading and translation, more than 95% of the text; the crown sign = Re; two name signs, the signature and a few words open. Dated 10 March 1413 from 'sesta indictione' with a king on the throne of Naples and Migliorati alive.

This project: DECODE R1858 and R4790 record pages fetched with the cookie: no document attached to either; R1858 p. 7 and R4790 P2 viewed, no gloss or decipherment. Cryptoole's 'solved/plaintext_attached' traced to a group status. No earlier reading of no. 12 found.

validation.notes: no sign-level transcription of no. 12 in the repository: George Lasry's report gives the reading and the key figure, not the CTTS transcription (asked for)

outcome.method_basis: Report, 17 Oct 2026: 'key recovered by Claude's own simulated annealing (865 symbols), then refined'; no decipherment, clear copy or filed key exists for no. 12.
outcome.fraction_read_source: key_lasry.jpg (the report's key figure) occurrence counts: 850 letter-sign + 4 RE occurrences of 865 symbols have a value; the 'Signoria Vostra?' sign (2), two name signs (3) and six unknown signs (6) do not. Key coverage, not sense; George's own estimate of the text read as sense is 'more than 95 %'.

credits.note: With CTTS and Claude, 15-17 Oct 2026: transcription by Claude, refined in CTTS; key recovered by Claude's own simulated annealing, then refined; reading, translation and dating.
credits.source: Email and report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026

gaps.item: two name signs and the 'Signoria Vostra?' sign
gaps.detail: 1-2 occurrences each; left open in the report

gaps.item: the signer ('Vescovi(?) de Fermo') and the two girls' fathers
a few (?) words and six unknown signs of one occurrence each
gaps.detail: single occurrences; no transcription in the repository to retry them

outcome.notes: Contributed result, filed from George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026; not re-derived here. fraction_coherent is his estimate ('more than 95 %'). Contamination: no earlier reading known (R1858's Decrypted status has no document behind it).

prior.where: None known. DECODE R1858 ('Siena keys and ciphers', 2020, owner 32), which holds a second photograph of no. 12, is marked Decrypted but has no document attached, and that photograph shows no gloss; R4790 is N/A with no documents (both checked 18 Oct 2026). The project's siena1421 notes (24 Sept 2026) had 'taken no. 12 as read' from R1858's status, without a reading. Cryptoole XX15XX-97 'solved/plaintext_attached' is a group status over the Concistoro records. Meister 1902 and the 1952 inventory print no reading.

human: George Lasry ran the work with CTTS and Claude: Claude transcribed, he refined the transcription in CTTS; Claude's own simulated annealing recovered the key, then refined; he wrote the reading, translation and historical context (report, 17 Oct 2026). This project filed the report and checked the DECODE record history.
